**Finding submitted: deviation (LICENSE), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations inspected:** the sole grant clause, section 2 (p0002); the licence definitions (p0003–p0014); the termination-consequence revocation (p0021); the use restrictions/third-party access bar (p0025); and the assignment clause (p0072).
- **Why it fails fallback:** the grant runs only to "Customer" (defined at p0000 as The Associated Press alone — no affiliate inclusion, so no duplicate coverage risk), with no affiliate/contractor path, and it is expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable", which as the specific provision defeats reliance on the general successor-assignment right in p0072.
- **Cure (one operation):** affiliates identified in written notice are added as licensees and the licence is made transferable to an M&A successor, by deleting only the conflicting "non-transferable, non-assignable," words and keeping the remainder of the grant verbatim.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the licence remains "revocable" and section 4(c)(ii) revokes it on termination — short of preferred, but deleting "revocable" would require collateral conforming edits to section 4(a)'s mutual convenience termination (which benefits us) and to 4(c)(ii), so the fallback edit is the shortest complete position.
